Case_18011/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) showing an ill-defined mass (arrow) at the porta hepatis extending into right hepatic lobe and coursing along common bile duct with intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.

description.short_caption: MRCP showing a mass at the porta hepatis with biliary ductal dilatation.
description.detailed_description: This MRCP image demonstrates an ill-defined mass at the porta hepatis, extending into the right hepatic lobe and along the common bile duct. There is associated intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation, visible as dilated tubular structures within the liver parenchyma. The mass appears to obstruct the biliary flow, which is a likely cause of the ductal dilation. The arrows point to the mass and dilated ducts for clarity.
visible_findings: ill-defined mass at the porta hepatis
extension into the right hepatic lobe
coursing along the common bile duct

Case_18011/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) where multiple trematodes (arrows) were directly visualized within biliary tract (Courtesy of USC+LAC GI Endoscopy Lab)

description.short_caption: ERCP showing multiple trematodes within the biliary tract.
description.detailed_description: This endoscopic image, obtained during an ERCP procedure, shows the biliary tract with multiple elongated, flat, worm-like structures consistent with trematodes. The organisms are highlighted by arrows and are located within the bile ducts. The surrounding mucosa appears inflamed and irregular, with bile-stained areas visible. The image demonstrates direct visualization of parasitic infestation.

Case_18011/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Fasciola hepatica fluke measuring 2.6 cm in length (Courtesy of Susan Butler-Wu, PhD, D(ABBM))

description.short_caption: Fasciola hepatica fluke measuring approximately 2.6 cm in length.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a preserved Fasciola hepatica fluke placed on a clear surface next to a ruler for scale. The fluke is leaf-shaped, with a flattened body and visible internal structures, including branching dark lines suggestive of its digestive or reproductive system. The ruler indicates the fluke's length is approximately 2.6 cm. The specimen is labeled as part of a pathology collection.

Case_18011/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Single trematode (arrow) within biliary tract at ERCP. (Courtesy of LAC +USC GI Endoscopy Lab)

description.short_caption: Endoscopic view of a single trematode within the biliary tract.
description.detailed_description: This endoscopic image shows the biliary tract with a single trematode (indicated by an arrow) visible within the lumen. The trematode appears as a flat, leaf-like structure with branching dark lines consistent with its internal anatomy. Surrounding mucosa appears erythematous, with some bile and debris visible. The image is captured during an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) procedure.
visible_findings: single trematode with branching internal structures
bile and debris in the lumen

Case_18011/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Fasciola hepatica egg measuring 130µM x 75µM obtained from stool sample. (Courtesy of Susan Butler-Wu, PhD, D(ABBM))

description.short_caption: Fasciola hepatica egg observed in stool sample under microscopy.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an oval-shaped egg of Fasciola hepatica, measuring approximately 130µm x 75µm, as observed under light microscopy. The egg has a smooth, thin shell and contains internal granular material. The background shows a light-stained field with some debris, consistent with a stool sample preparation. The image is labeled with a copyright notice from IDSA 2018.
